pois.name: Shaniwar Wada
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 9:30 AM - 6:30 PM (Light & Sound Show in Evening)
pois.description: Grand 18th-century seat of the Peshwas of the Maratha Empire, featuring historic Delhi Darwaza and fortified ramparts.
pois.history: Built in 1732 by Peshwa Baji Rao I. The fort witnessed the rise and glory of the Maratha Empire with its massive teakwood courtyards.

pois.name: Aga Khan Palace
pois.description: Majestic palace with Italian arches and sprawling lawns; historic site of the Quit India Movement.
pois.history: Built in 1892 by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III to support famine-affected locals. Served as Mahatma Gandhi's internment site in 1942.

pois.name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
pois.description: Ancient monolithic rock-cut cave temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, carved out of a single basalt rock.
pois.history: Carved during the Rashtrakuta period in the 8th century AD, featuring massive stone pillars and a circular Nandi mandapa.

pois.name: Lal Mahal
pois.description: Historic red-brick palace where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj spent his formative childhood years.
pois.history: Originally constructed in 1630 by Shahaji Bhosale for his wife Jijabai and young Shivaji. Historic site of Shivaji Maharaj's legendary encounter with Shaista Khan.

pois.name: Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum
pois.description: Astonishing collection of over 20,000 Indian artifacts, musical instruments, and the Mastani Mahal replica.
pois.history: Created by Dr. D.G. Kelkar in memory of his only son Dinkar. Houses 14th-century weapons, brass lamps, and intricately carved doors.

pois.name: Sinhagad Fort
pois.description: Majestic hilltop fort famous for the heroic Battle of Sinhagad (Tanaji Malusare), authentic pithla-bhakri, and panoramic Sahyadri views.
pois.history: Known as Kondhana, renamed Sinhagad ('Lion's Fort') by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1670 in honour of general Tanaji Malusare.

pois.name: Bedekar Misal
pois.description: Authentic sweet-tangy Puneri misal with fresh crunchy farsan, sliced bread, and fiery family tarri spices.
pois.history: Serving Pune's most celebrated traditional misal pav recipe since 1948 in the heart of old Narayan Peth.

pois.name: Cafe Goodluck
pois.description: Legendary Irani cafe famous for Bun Maska, Keema Pav, caramel custard, and spicy Katakir dishes.
pois.history: Established in 1935, it is Pune's oldest active Irani cafe, frequented by generations of FTII and Fergusson students.

pois.name: FC Road Street Food & Vada Pav
pois.description: Crispy piping-hot batata vada pav, grilled cheese sandwiches, sabudana vada, and cutting chai surrounded by college energy.
pois.history: Fergusson College Road has been Pune's culinary and street shopping nerve center for decades.

pois.name: JM Road Street Food & Juice Stalls
pois.description: Vibrant avenue renowned for butter-drenched pav bhaji, thick seasonal Sitaphal milkshakes, and dosas.
pois.history: Named after Justice Jangli Maharaj, this wide illuminated avenue has been Pune's food pride since the 1960s.

pois.name: Sarasbaug Chowpatty & Bhel Katta
pois.description: Iconic open-air chaat chowpatty serving authentic Oli Bhel, SPDP (Sev Potato Dahi Puri), and Matka Kulfi.
pois.history: Located opposite the 18th-century Talyatla Ganpati lake temple built by Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa.

pois.name: Vaishali Restaurant
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 7:00 AM - 11:00 PM (Signature Filter Coffee & Mysore Masala Dosa)
pois.description: Pune's most revered cultural institution serving Mysore Masala Dosa, SPDP, Cheese Uttapam, and filter coffee in a garden courtyard.
pois.history: Established in 1949 by Jagannath Shetty (initially Madras Cafe), frequented by scholars, politicians, FTII filmmakers, and students.

pois.name: FC Road (Fashion Street)
pois.description: Bustling open-air shopping sidewalk offering trendy western wear, Kolhapuri chappals, junk jewellery, and bags.
pois.history: Famous student fashion shopping hub operating alongside prestigious universities since the 1980s.

pois.name: MG Road (Camp Shopping District)
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM (Walking Plaza on Weekend Evenings)
pois.description: Pune's historic commercial boulevard featuring lifestyle brand showrooms, shoe stores, and street fashion alleyways.
pois.history: Originally British Cantonment Main Street, retaining classic colonial arcades and century-old bakeries.

pois.name: Hong Kong Lane (Fashion & Accessories)
pois.description: Famous narrow shopping alley brimming with trendy sunglasses, phone accessories, cosmetics, watches, and belts.
pois.history: Pune's original imported gadgets and accessories market established by local traders near Deccan.

pois.name: Koregaon Park Boutique Area
pois.description: Lush tree-canopied lanes with indie fashion studios, organic fabric stores, handmade jewellery, and artisanal home decor.
pois.history: Upscale residential quarter transformed into a bohemian luxury boutique district.

pois.name: Phoenix Marketcity Pune
pois.description: Over 350+ global fashion labels (Zara, H&M, Sephora), PVR IMAX multiplex, and sprawling international food court.
pois.history: Pune's largest destination mall built to serve the eastern IT and airport residential corridor.

pois.name: Amanora Mall & Town Centre
pois.description: Open-air landscaped mall featuring global apparel brands, central water oasis, bowling alleys, and open-air concerts.
pois.history: Modern township lifestyle hub connecting Hadapsar with Magarpatta Cybercity.

pois.name: The Pavillion Mall (SB Road)
pois.description: Upscale multi-story fashion hub with top international cosmetic brands, Marks & Spencer, lifestyle cafes, and PVR ICON.
pois.history: Flagship retail destination on Senapati Bapat Road offering convenient shopping for central Pune.

pois.name: Shreemant Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati
pois.description: Pune's most revered and beloved Ganpati temple, adorned with solid gold and deep historical devotion.
pois.history: Founded in 1893 by sweetmaker Dagdusheth Gadve and his wife Lakshmibai after Lokmanya Tilak's public Ganeshotsav appeal.

pois.name: Osho International Meditation Resort
pois.description: World-famous Zen gardens, black marble pyramids, and meditation spaces amidst tranquil green canopies.
pois.history: Founded in 1974 by Osho Rajneesh; attracts international travelers seeking mindfulness in lush Koregaon Park.

pois.name: Fergusson College Road & Campus
pois.description: Lush 65-acre campus with Victorian Gothic stone buildings, botanical garden, and lively intellectual atmosphere.
pois.history: Founded in 1885 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar; alma mater to Indian freedom fighters and thinkers.

pois.name: Baner-Balewadi High Street
pois.description: Bustling cosmopolitan strip lined with microbreweries, rooftop lounges, live music venues, and European bistros.
pois.history: Developed into Western Pune's tech and lifestyle hub connecting Hinjawadi IT Park with the city.

pois.name: Pu La Deshpande Okayama Friendship Garden
pois.description: Breathtaking Japanese stroll garden inspired by the 300-year-old Kōraku-en in Okayama, featuring natural streams and wooden footbridges.
pois.history: Named after Maharashtra's iconic writer P.L. Deshpande, symbolizing the sister-city friendship between Pune and Okayama.

pois.name: Savitribai Phule Pune University Campus
pois.type: Oxford of the East & Colonial Heritage
pois.description: Expansive 411-acre campus shaded by century-old banyan trees, housing the iconic colonial Main Building with its 100-ft stone clock tower.
pois.history: Established in 1949, originally Governor's Monsoon Residence during British rule; earned Pune its title 'Oxford of the East'.

pois.name: The Heritage Backpacker Pods
pois.description: Chic, highly rated hostel nestled in quiet tree-lined Koregaon Park with keycard entry, female dorms, cafe, and high-speed Wi-Fi.
pois.history: Transformed 1970s bungalow preserving Pune's classic garden-city vibe with modern solar amenities.

pois.name: Deccan Business Suites & Residency
pois.description: Centrally located hotel walking distance to FC Road, offering comfortable AC rooms, complimentary breakfast, and secure parking.
pois.history: Prime hospitality establishment catering to academic visitors, researchers, and culture seekers.

pois.name: JW Marriott Hotel Pune
pois.description: World-class 5-star luxury with heated infinity pool, Quan Spa, Italian restaurant Alto Vino, and rooftop lounge Paasha.
pois.history: Pune's architectural landmark on SB Road, known for hosting international summits and celebrities.

pois.name: The Westin Pune Koregaon Park
pois.description: Opulent riverside retreat featuring Heavenly Beds, rejuvenating Heavenly Spa, fine dining, and vibrant nightlife at The Market.
pois.history: Pioneering luxury hotel in Koregaon Park's tech and expatriate hub alongside the Mula-Mutha river.

pois.name: Ibis Pune Viman Nagar
pois.description: Sleek, modern hotel minutes from Pune International Airport and Phoenix Marketcity with fast Wi-Fi and 24/7 fitness center.
pois.history: Popular choice for business travellers and weekend shoppers visiting eastern Pune.

pois.name: Gateway of India
pois.description: Iconic basalt arch overlooking the Arabian Sea, built in 1924, facing the grand Taj Mahal Palace Hotel.
pois.history: Erected to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary at Apollo Bunder in 1911.

pois.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)
pois.description: Breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage terminus featuring high Victorian Gothic design blended with traditional Indian motifs.
pois.history: Designed by F.W. Stevens, completed in 1887 to commemorate Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee.

pois.name: Elephanta Caves
pois.description: UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave temples dating to the 5th-7th centuries, renowned for the 20-foot high Trimurti sculpture.
pois.history: Constructed during the Rashtrakuta and Kalachuri dynasties on Gharapuri island in Mumbai Harbour.

pois.name: Kanheri Caves
pois.description: Over 100 basalt rock-cut Buddhist caves nestled deep in lush national park forests with prayer halls and stupas.
pois.history: Thrived from 1st century BCE to 10th century CE as a major Buddhist learning center along ancient trade routes.

pois.name: Castella de Aguada (Bandra Fort)
pois.description: Historic coastal fortress ruins offering sweeping panoramas of the Arabian Sea and the modern Bandra-Worli Sea Link.
pois.history: Constructed by the Portuguese in 1640 as a defensive guard post overlooking Mahim Bay.

pois.name: Flora Fountain & Heritage Mile
pois.description: Exquisite 1864 sculpted Portland stone fountain representing Flora, Roman goddess of nature, at the heart of colonial Mumbai.
pois.history: Erected in honor of Sir Bartle Frere, Governor of Bombay; restored meticulously by INTACH.

pois.name: Girgaon Chowpatty Street Food
pois.description: Famous public beach renowned for sizzling tava pav bhaji, bhelpuri, sev puri, and rich Badshah kulfi falooda.
pois.history: The quintessential birthplace of Bombay bhelpuri culture and Ganpati Visarjan festivities since the late 1800s.

pois.name: Britannia & Co. Restaurant
pois.description: Century-old culinary landmark famous for Mutton Berry Pulao, Sali Boti, caramel custard, and vintage heritage ambiance.
pois.history: Founded in 1923 by Rashid Kohinoor, serving generations of Mumbai food lovers in colonial Ballard Estate.

pois.name: Mohammed Ali Road (Minara Masjid)
pois.type: Iconic Mughlai Kebabs, Nalli Nihari & Malpua
pois.description: Electrifying street culinary lane packed with sizzling seekh kebabs, rich slow-cooked Nalli Nihari, and rabdi-topped malpua.
pois.history: World-famous food street celebrated during Ramzan and year-round as Mumbai's ultimate nocturnal culinary paradise.

pois.name: Kyani & Co. Bakery & Cafe
pois.type: Oldest Surviving Irani Cafe in Mumbai
pois.description: Timeless Irani cafe serving Bun Maska, hot Irani Chai, Kheema Pav, and mawa cakes with checkered tablecloths and high ceilings.
pois.history: Established in 1904 by Mr. Khodaram Marezban, standing unchanged for over 120 years opposite Edward Cinema.

pois.name: Bademiya Kebab Gali
pois.description: World-famous late-night street kebab destination with charcoal grills serving chicken bhuna rolls, baida roti, and seekh kebabs.
pois.history: Started in 1942 by Mohammad Yaseen on a small handcart with a ₹20 loan from a naval officer.

pois.name: Gajalee Seafood Restaurant
pois.description: Celebrated coastal dining haven famous for Tandoori Crab, Butter Garlic Lobster, Surmai fry, and Sol Kadhi.
pois.history: A legendary culinary institution preserving traditional coastal Maharashtrian seafood recipes for decades.

pois.name: Colaba Causeway Fashion Street
pois.description: Lively commercial corridor packed with vintage jewelry stalls, leather bags, sunglasses, and Cafe Mondegar.
pois.history: One of Mumbai's historic causeways connecting Colaba island to the mainland since 1838.

pois.name: Linking Road & Hill Road Bandra
pois.description: Queen of the Suburbs shopping capital lined with trendy streetwear stalls, shoe plazas, chic cafes, and celebrity boutiques.
pois.history: Bandra's fashion nerve center connecting traditional Portuguese villages with contemporary Bollywood style.

pois.name: High Street Phoenix & Palladium
pois.description: Premier upscale shopping hub with international luxury flagships (Gucci, Chanel, Zara), fine dining, and multiplex cinema.
pois.history: Transformed from defunct textile mills into Mumbai's glitziest modern retail and entertainment epicenter.

pois.name: Crawford Market (Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai)
pois.description: Historic market famous for Lockwood Kipling stone friezes, imported chocolates, home decor, dry fruits, and fragrances.
pois.history: Completed in 1869, designed by William Emerson; the first building in India lit by electricity in 1882.

pois.name: Chor Bazaar (Mutton Street)
pois.description: Fascinating 150-year-old market packed with Bollywood movie posters, antique gramophones, brass nautical clocks, and vintage furniture.
pois.history: Originally named Shor Bazaar (Noisy Market) by the British; gradually became world-renowned for rare antiquities.

pois.name: Marine Drive Promenade
pois.description: 3.6-kilometer-long C-shaped boulevard along the coast offering magnificent sunset vistas and Mumbai skyline views.
pois.history: Constructed in the 1920s as part of the Back Bay Reclamation scheme with classic Art Deco architecture.

pois.name: Kala Ghoda Art District & Museum
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM (Kala Ghoda Festival in Feb)
pois.description: Mumbai's premier cultural crescent packed with art galleries (Jehangir Art Gallery), indie designer shops, and heritage cafes.
pois.history: Named after the black stone statue of King Edward VII on horseback that once stood at the junction.

pois.name: Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir
pois.description: One of India's wealthiest and most revered temples dedicated to Lord Ganesha, featuring a gold-plated inner sanctum.
pois.history: Originally consecrated on 19 November 1801 by Laxman Vithu and Deubai Patil.

pois.name: Haji Ali Dargah
pois.description: Spectacular 15th-century Indo-Islamic shrine and mosque situated on an islet 500 meters off the coast into the Arabian Sea.
pois.history: Constructed in 1431 in memory of the wealthy merchant Sayyed Peer Haji Ali Shah Bukhari.

pois.name: Bandra Bandstand & Mannat Promenade
pois.type: Celebrity Sea Walk & Rocky Coastal Promenade
pois.description: Scenic 1.2-kilometer sea-facing walkway famous for Bollywood celebrity residences (Shah Rukh Khan's Mannat), sea breeze, and food stalls.
pois.history: Beloved promenade hosting the Walk of the Stars commemorating legendary Indian cinematic figures.

pois.name: The Taj Mahal Palace Mumbai
pois.description: Legendary 1903 landmark hotel featuring grand floating staircases, vaulted alabaster ceilings, and Wasabi by Morimoto.
pois.history: Commissioned by Jamsetji Tata and opened on 16 December 1903 as India's first luxury hotel.

pois.name: The St. Regis Mumbai
pois.description: India's tallest luxury hotel tower overlooking the Mahalaxmi Racecourse and sea with celebrated rooftop lounges (Asilo).
pois.history: The definitive modern luxury hub in central Mumbai connecting directly into the Palladium retail complex.

pois.name: Trident Hotel Nariman Point
pois.description: 35-storey oceanfront landmark with panoramic Queen's Necklace vistas, premier Italian dining at Frangipani, and luxury suites.
pois.history: A staple of South Mumbai's business elite and international diplomats for over four decades.

pois.name: India Gate & Kartavya Path
pois.description: Soaring 42-meter triumphal sandstone arch honoring 84,000 fallen soldiers, fronting the sprawling fountains of Kartavya Path.
pois.history: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, completed in 1931 with the Amar Jawan Jyoti flame burning eternal.

pois.name: Qutub Minar & Mehrauli Complex
pois.description: 73-meter towering fluted red sandstone minaret, Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, and the mysterious rust-resistant 4th-century Iron Pillar.
pois.history: Initiated by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192 and finished by Iltutmish; masterpiece of early Indo-Islamic engineering.

pois.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
pois.description: Massive red sandstone fortress that served as the primary residence of the Mughal Emperors for nearly 200 years.
pois.history: Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638 upon shifting the capital from Agra to Delhi (Shahjahanabad).

pois.name: Humayun's Tomb & Sunder Nursery
pois.description: Magnificent red sandstone garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal, flanked by the 90-acre heritage ecological haven Sunder Nursery.
pois.history: Built in 1570 by Empress Bega Begum; pioneer of Mughal double-dome garden tomb architecture in India.

pois.name: Jama Masjid Delhi
pois.description: One of the largest mosques in India, featuring four minarets, three marble domes, and a courtyard holding 25,000 worshippers.
pois.history: Constructed between 1650 and 1656 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan with 5,000 artisans.

pois.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
pois.description: Atmospheric 60-meter-long stepwell with 108 stone steps descending through arched corridors in the heart of modern Delhi.
pois.history: Believed to have been originally built by Maharaja Agrasen and rebuilt during the Tughlaq era in the 14th century.

pois.name: Paranthe Wali Gali (Chandni Chowk)
pois.description: Narrow historic lane celebrated for authentic ghee-fried paranthas stuffed with rabdi, dry fruits, paneer, and served with sweet pumpkin curry.
pois.history: Began in the 1870s with Pt. Gaya Prasad Paranthewale; visited by national leaders from Nehru to Indira Gandhi.

pois.name: Karim's Historic Mughlai (Gali Kababian)
pois.type: Royal Mughal Mutton Burra & Seekh Kebabs
pois.description: Legendary culinary institution established by royal Mughal cooks, famous for Mutton Korma, Burra Kebabs, and Khamiri Roti.
pois.history: Founded in 1913 by Haji Karimuddin after the fall of the Mughal court to serve royal recipes to the common people.

pois.name: Moti Mahal Daryaganj
pois.type: Birthplace of Butter Chicken & Dal Makhani
pois.description: Iconic restaurant credited with inventing world-renowned Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) and slow-simmered Dal Makhani.
pois.history: Established in 1947 by Kundan Lal Gujral following Partition, bringing tandoori gastronomy to the global stage.

pois.name: Kake Da Vakeel & Kake Da Hotel
pois.type: Hearty Punjabi Dhaba Curries & Tandoori Roti
pois.description: Bustling Punjabi culinary landmark famous for rich Dahi Meat, Keema Kaleji, Butter Chicken, and warm rumali rotis.
pois.history: Operating since 1931 in Connaught Place, serving authentic rustic Punjabi gravies to generations of Delhiites.

pois.name: Sita Ram Diwan Chand Paharganj
pois.description: Unrivaled breakfast institution serving fluffy paneer-stuffed bhaturas with spicy, aromatic slow-cooked chole and pickled chilies.
pois.history: Serving delicious breakfast since the 1950s, crowned as the golden standard of Delhi Chole Bhature.

pois.name: Pandara Road Food Gali
pois.type: Late Night North Indian & Kebab Feast
pois.description: Delhi's favorite upscale late-night culinary street featuring Gulati, Havemore, and Ichiban for nocturnal family feasts.
pois.history: Centuries-long culinary hub frequented by politicians, celebrities, and late-night foodies near India Gate.

pois.name: Connaught Place (Inner & Outer Circle)
pois.description: Magnificent circular Georgian-style white colonnades housing international fashion flagships, bookshops, and Palika underground bazaar.
pois.history: Constructed in 1933 by Robert Tor Russell; named after Prince Arthur, 1st Duke of Connaught.

pois.name: Dilli Haat INA Crafts Village
pois.description: Open-air traditional rural village market showcasing authentic handloom sarees, terracotta craft, Kashmiri shawls, and regional state food stalls.
pois.history: Established by Delhi Tourism in 1994 to provide direct urban marketplace access to rural Indian artisans.

pois.name: Khan Market Luxury Precinct
pois.description: Exclusive U-shaped enclave of indie designer boutiques (Good Earth, Forest Essentials), heritage bookshops (Bahrisons), and gourmet cafes.
pois.history: Established in 1951, named in honor of freedom fighter Khan Abdul Jabbar Khan.

pois.name: Sarojini Nagar Fashion Street
pois.type: Legendary Export Surplus & Budget Wardrobe Market
pois.description: India's most popular export-surplus flea market packed with high-street fashion, denim jackets, bags, and sunglasses at unbelievable bargains.
pois.history: Named after freedom fighter Sarojini Naidu, serving students and stylists as India's premier fashion hunting ground.

pois.name: Select CITYWALK Mall Saket
pois.type: Premier South Delhi Retail & Entertainment Mall
pois.description: State-of-the-art 1.3 million sq ft shopping center with open-air plazas, luxury global apparel, beauty flagships, and gourmet dining.
pois.history: Opened in 2007 as Delhi's premier modern lifestyle and fashion shopping landmark.

pois.name: Hauz Khas Village & Lake Ruins
pois.description: Enchanting juxtaposition of medieval madrasa ruins overlooking a royal water tank, flanked by bohemian art galleries and rooftop bistros.
pois.history: Commissioned by Alauddin Khalji in 1295 to supply water to Siri Fort; later expanded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

pois.name: Lotus Temple (Bahá'í House of Worship)
pois.type: Iconic Pure White Marble Lotus Architecture
pois.description: Architectural wonder sculpted from Greek Pentelikon marble into 27 lotus petals surrounded by 9 serene reflection ponds.
pois.history: Designed by Iranian-Canadian architect Fariborz Sahba, consecrated in 1986 as a sanctuary open to all faiths.

pois.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
pois.description: Radiant marble Sikh sanctuary featuring a golden dome, sacred holy pool (Sarovar), and a mega-kitchen serving free langar to 30,000 people daily.
pois.history: Originally a bungalow of Raja Jai Singh in the 17th century; associated with the 8th Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan.

pois.name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA)
pois.type: Premier Modern & Contemporary Indian Art Museum
pois.description: Palatial museum housing over 17,000 landmark works by Raja Ravi Varma, Amrita Sher-Gil, Rabindranath Tagore, and MF Husain.
pois.history: Inaugurated in 1954 in the former royal winter residence of the Maharaja of Jaipur.

pois.name: Lodhi Art District (Open Air Mural Gallery)
pois.type: India's First Public Street Art District
pois.description: Transformative public art project with over 50 mammoth building-sized murals painted by renowned global and Indian street artists.
pois.history: Curated by St+art India Foundation transforming 1940s government housing facades into an open-air art museum.

pois.name: The Imperial New Delhi
pois.type: Legendary 1930s Art Deco & Victorian Heritage Hotel
pois.description: Iconic colonial luxury hotel boasting palm-lined driveways, original 19th-century British artwork collections, and Spice Route restaurant.
pois.history: Opened in 1936 by Lord Willingdon; venue of historic independence negotiations with Gandhi, Nehru, and Jinnah.

pois.name: The Leela Palace New Delhi
pois.description: Opulent modern palace hotel in the diplomatic district featuring Murano chandeliers, rooftop infinity pool, and Le Cirque fine dining.
pois.history: Flagship property embodying classical Lutyens New Delhi grandeur with contemporary Indian luxury.

pois.name: Taj Mahal Hotel (Number One Mansingh)
pois.description: Pink Dholpur sandstone luxury landmark celebrated for Machan, House of Ming, and hosting international heads of state.
pois.history: A hallmark of Indian hospitality in Lutyens Delhi for over four decades.

pois.name: Bangalore Palace
pois.description: Majestic 19th-century royal palace modeled after Windsor Castle, featuring fortified towers, battlements, and wood carvings.
pois.history: Acquired and expanded in 1884 by Chamarajendra Wadiyar X, Maharaja of Mysore.

pois.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
pois.description: Stunning two-storey palace built entirely from teakwood with ornamental pillars, cusped arches, and floral wall frescoes.
pois.history: Begun by Hyder Ali and completed in 1791 by Tipu Sultan, who described it as the Abode of Happiness.

pois.name: Devanahalli Fort
pois.description: Massive stone fortress with 12 semi-circular bastions spread across 20 acres, marking the birthplace of Tipu Sultan.
pois.history: Originally built in 1501 by Malla Byre Gowda; heavily fortified by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan in the late 18th century.

pois.name: Bull Temple (Nandi Temple)
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 6:00 AM - 8:30 PM (Kadalekai Parishe Festival in Nov)
pois.description: Ancient Dravidian temple housing a colossal 4.5-meter-high monolithic stone statue of Nandi, the sacred bull of Shiva.
pois.history: Constructed in 1537 by Kempe Gowda I, the visionary founder of Bengaluru city.

pois.name: Mayo Hall & Colonial Cantonment Walk
pois.description: Imposing two-storey heritage edifice with architraves, pediments, and Corinthian columns commemorating the 4th Viceroy of India.
pois.history: Completed in 1883 in memory of Lord Mayo, offering panoramic vistas of the Cantonment racecourse.

pois.name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
pois.description: Mystical monolithic rock-cut cave temple famous for its astronomical precision during Makar Sankranti when sunlight illuminates Shiva's idol.
pois.history: Carved in the 9th century and revitalized by Kempe Gowda I with massive stone disc sculptures.

pois.name: Mavalli Tiffin Room (MTR Lalbagh)
pois.type: Legendary 1924 Rava Idli & South Indian Thali
pois.description: Century-old culinary legend celebrated for pure ghee Masala Dosa, inventor of the Rava Idli, and authentic silver-thali feasts.
pois.history: Founded in 1924 by the Maiya brothers; invented Rava Idli during WWII rice shortages.

pois.name: Vidyarthi Bhavan Gandhi Bazaar
pois.type: Heritage Golden Crispy Butter Masala Dosa
pois.description: Iconic 1943 tiffin room legendary for waiters balancing towering stacks of thick, golden-brown, melt-in-the-mouth Benne Masala Dosas.
pois.history: Started as a student canteen in 1943, frequented by Kannada literary giants like DV Gundappa and Kuvempu.

pois.name: VV Puram Food Street (Thindi Beedi)
pois.type: Legendary Vegetarian Night Street Food Haven
pois.description: Electrifying pedestrian food lane packed with 20+ street stalls serving hot Akki Rotti, Paddus, Capsicum Bajjis, and Floating Rasgullas.
pois.history: Bengaluru's premier pure-vegetarian nocturnal street food institution for over 50 years.

pois.name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
pois.type: Pillow-Soft Idli, Crispy Vada & Coconut Chutney
pois.description: Legendary standing-only tiffin counter serving steaming soft idlis submerged in free-flowing mint coconut chutney and strong filter coffee.
pois.history: Established in 1965 by KV Nagesh Rao, maintaining a simple, four-item perfected menu for 60 years.

pois.name: Toit Brewpub Indiranagar
pois.description: Iconic multi-level craft brewpub that ignited Bengaluru's craft beer revolution, serving Tint-in-Toit wheat beer and woodfired sourdough pizzas.
pois.history: Founded in 2010, establishing Bengaluru as the Craft Beer Capital of India.

pois.name: Nagarjuna Andhra Meals Residency Rd
pois.type: Spicy Authentic Andhra Banana Leaf Thali
pois.description: Fiery and lavish Andhra banana leaf meals featuring unlimited rice, Gunpowder (Podi), ghee, Pappu dal, and signature Andhra Chili Chicken.
pois.history: Started in 1984 on Residency Road; an enduring culinary obsession for Bengaluru techies and food lovers.

pois.name: Commercial Street & Brigade Road
pois.description: Densely packed shopping avenues lined with bridal silks, customized tailoring, silver jewellery, footwear lanes, and global apparel flagships.
pois.history: The historical retail hub of the Bangalore Cantonment developed during the British era.

pois.name: 100 Feet Road Indiranagar
pois.description: India's most valuable retail high-street lined with premier global streetwear flagships, artisanal lifestyle stores, and artisanal bakeries.
pois.history: Transformed from a quiet residential layout into India's trendiest lifestyle and boutique corridor.

pois.name: UB City Luxury Mall & Promenade
pois.type: India's First Luxury Mall & Penthouse Dining
pois.description: Pinnacle of luxury shopping featuring Louis Vuitton, Burberry, Rolex, contemporary art galleries, and open-air rooftop lounges.
pois.history: Joint venture between UB Group and Prestige Group, redefining India's high-net-worth retail experiences.

pois.name: Chickpet Wholesale Silk Saree Bazaar
pois.description: Historic labyrinth of lanes renowned for wholesale pure Mysore silk, Kanjivaram zari sarees, and traditional bridal jewelry.
pois.history: Established in the 16th century by Kempe Gowda I as Bengaluru's original commercial merchant market.

pois.name: Phoenix Marketcity Whitefield
pois.type: Massive East Bengaluru Lifestyle & Retail Hub
pois.description: Sprawling shopping metropolis with over 300 international brands, IMAX theaters, expansive food courts, and open-air musical concerts.
pois.history: The cornerstone of Whitefield's modern IT corridor lifestyle since 2011.

pois.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden & Glass House
pois.description: Legendary 240-acre garden home to centuries-old trees, a serene lake, Kempe Gowda tower on 3,000-million-year-old rock, and Victorian Glass House.
pois.history: Commissioned in 1760 by Hyder Ali and completed by Tipu Sultan; modeled after Crystal Palace in London.

pois.name: Cubbon Park & Attara Kacheri
pois.description: Lush canopy park with over 6,000 trees, bamboo groves, red-brick High Court (Attara Kacheri), and State Central Library.
pois.history: Created in 1870 by Major General Richard Sankey, Chief Engineer of Mysore State.

pois.name: Church Street & Blossom Book House
pois.description: Paved pedestrian street famous for legendary second-hand bookshop Blossom Book House, indie cafes, artists, and live street music.
pois.history: Paved under the TenderSURE model creating Bengaluru's most walkable and vibrant cultural strip.

pois.name: Sri Sri Radha Krishna Temple (ISKCON Bangalore)
pois.description: One of the largest ISKCON temples in the world, perched atop Hare Krishna Hill with gold-plated flagstaff, fountains, and kirtans.
pois.history: Inaugurated in May 1997 by the ninth President of India, Dr. Shankar Dayal Sharma.

pois.name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA Bengaluru)
pois.description: Stunning Manikyavelu Mansion surrounded by reflection pools and ancient trees displaying modern Indian art and sculpture.
pois.history: Once the residence of Raja Manikyavelu Mudaliar; restored into a world-class art gallery in 2009.

pois.name: The Leela Palace Bengaluru
pois.type: Grand Art Deco & Royal Vijayanagara Palace Hotel
pois.description: Extravagant palace hotel inspired by the Royal Palace of Mysore and Vijayanagara Empire with 7 acres of lush gardens and Zen Japanese dining.
pois.history: Built by Captain C.P. Krishnan Nair; an enduring gold standard of Indian luxury hospitality.

pois.name: ITC Gardenia, a Luxury Collection Hotel
pois.type: Eco-Luxury Five-Star & Peacocks in Central City
pois.description: LEED Platinum-certified luxury hotel inspired by Bengaluru's gardens, home to the award-winning Edo Japanese restaurant and Windmills.
pois.history: A hallmark of responsible green luxury in India adjacent to Cubbon Park.

pois.name: Taj West End, Bengaluru
pois.description: Bengaluru's oldest hotel set amid 20 acres of tropical flora with a 150-year-old banyan tree, Blue Ginger Vietnamese dining, and colonial charm.
pois.history: Founded in 1887 as Bronson's Boarding House; Bangalore's timeless colonial oasis.

pois.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Best Morning Golden Hour Photos)
pois.description: World-famous 5-storey pink sandstone façade with 953 intricately carved jharokhas (windows) designed like Lord Krishna's crown.
pois.history: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh to allow royal women to observe street life without being seen.

pois.name: Amer Fort (Amber Palace)
pois.description: Imposing hilltop citadel overlooking Maota Lake, famous for the dazzling Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) and elephant pathway.
pois.history: Constructed in 1592 by Raja Man Singh I; the former royal stronghold of the Kachwaha Rajputs.

pois.name: City Palace Jaipur
pois.description: Grand complex of fusion Rajput, Mughal, and European architecture with Pritam Niwas Chowk peacock gates and royal armory.
pois.history: Established by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727 when he founded the planned city of Jaipur.

pois.name: Nahargarh Fort
pois.type: Aravalli Hilltop Sunset Fort & Madhavendra Bhawan
pois.bestTimeToVisit: 4:30 PM - 7:30 PM (Panoramic Sunset over Pink City)
pois.description: Dramatic fort standing on the edge of the Aravalli Hills offering sensational sunset views of Jaipur city lights, Padao open-air cafe, and stepwells.
pois.history: Built in 1734 by Sawai Jai Singh II as a retreat fort forming a defensive ring with Amer and Jaigarh.

pois.name: Jaigarh Fort (Victory Fort)
pois.type: Massive Military Fortress & World's Largest Cannon on Wheels
pois.description: Undaunted military fort perched on the Hill of Eagles housing Jaivana — the world's largest cannon on wheels — and subterranean water vaults.
pois.history: Built in 1726 by Sawai Jai Singh II to defend Amer Palace; never conquered in battle.

pois.name: Jal Mahal (Water Palace)
pois.type: Submerged Rajput Palace in Man Sagar Lake
pois.description: Mesmerizing 5-storey red sandstone palace standing in the middle of Man Sagar Lake, with four storeys submerged underwater.
pois.history: Built in 1750 by Maharaja Madho Singh I as a duck-hunting lodge and summer retreat.

pois.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB Johari Bazaar)
pois.type: Legendary Rajasthani Ghewar, Pyaaz Kachori & Thali
pois.description: 1727 sweetshop and restaurant world-famous for Paneer Ghewar, piping hot crisp Pyaaz Kachori, and royal Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma.
pois.history: Founded in 1727 alongside the founding of Jaipur, making it one of India's oldest operating culinary institutions.

pois.name: Chokhi Dhani Ethnic Resort & Village Feast
pois.type: Immersion Rajasthani Village Experience & Royal Thali
pois.description: Immersive 5-star ethnic cultural village offering Kalbelia folk dances, puppet shows, camel rides, and unlimited multi-course Dal Baati Churma feasts on floor cushions.
pois.history: Created in 1989 to preserve and celebrate rural Rajasthani heritage, music, and royal culinary hospitality.

pois.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
pois.type: India's Most Famous Mawa & Pyaaz Kachori
pois.description: Legendary sweetshop selling over 10,000 freshly fried golden Pyaaz and Mawa Kachoris daily, served with tangy tamarind chutney.
pois.history: A beloved institution for over 70 years, the essential snack stop for every traveler arriving at Jaipur Station.

pois.name: Handi Restaurant MI Road
pois.type: Authentic Royal Laal Maas & Handi Meat
pois.description: Celebrated royal dining house famous for authentic slow-cooked Rajasthani Laal Maas (spicy red chili mutton) and charcoal Handi Meat.
pois.history: Preserving authentic Rajput royal hunting camp recipes on MI Road since 1984.

pois.name: Lassiwala (Since 1944)
pois.description: Legendary shop serving thick, creamy, slow-churned sweet lassi topped with a thick dollop of clotted cream (malai) in earthen kulhads.
pois.history: Founded in 1944 at Shop 312 MI Road; a ritual morning pilgrimage for tourists and locals alike.

pois.name: 1135 AD Amer Palace
pois.description: Fine dining restaurant situated inside the fortified walls of Amer Fort featuring gold-leaf walls, silver cutlery, live sitar, and thalis.
pois.history: Named after the year the Kachwaha clan founded the Amber kingdom; an unforgettable regal banquet experience.

pois.name: Johari Bazaar (Jewellers' Market)
pois.description: World-famous gemstone and jewellery market packed with certified emeralds, rubies, Kundan polki necklaces, and traditional Bandhani sarees.
pois.history: Founded in 1727 with designated havelis for royal master jewelers patronized by the Maharaja of Jaipur.

pois.name: Bapu Bazaar & Link Road
pois.description: Pink-painted arcade bazaar famous for camel leather embroidered Mojaris, featherlight Jaipuri Razai (quilts), and Sanganeri block-print kurtas.
pois.history: The undisputed heartbeat of traditional Rajasthani retail and souvenir shopping in the Pink City.

pois.name: Tripolia Bazaar & Maniharon ka Rasta
pois.description: Historic market lane famous for artisans melting and crafting intricate Lacquer bangles studded with glass crystals right before your eyes.
pois.history: Home to the traditional Muslim Lac bangle-making families who have supplied Jaipur royal brides for three centuries.

pois.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing & Boutique
pois.type: Artisanal Wooden Block Printing & Ethical Fashion
pois.description: Housed in a restored 16th-century haveli dedicated to preserving traditional hand block printing, featuring master artisan live demonstrations.
pois.history: Established by Anokhi to sustain rural craft communities and bring ethical handloom fashion to global acclaim.

pois.name: World Trade Park (WTP Jaipur)
pois.description: Iconic blue glass twin-tower modern shopping complex featuring floating bridges, international fashion flagships, and cineplexes.
pois.history: Inaugurated in 2012 by Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan; recipient of best modern architecture awards.

pois.name: Jantar Mantar Astronomical Observatory
pois.description: UNESCO World Heritage site containing 19 architectural astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial (Vrihat Samrat Yantra).
pois.history: Constructed by astronomer Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1734; measures time accurate to two seconds.

pois.name: Albert Hall Museum (Central Museum)
pois.description: Oldest museum in Rajasthan housing miniature paintings, Egyptian mummy, Persian carpets, and flock of pigeons in Ram Niwas Garden.
pois.history: Designed by Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob; foundation laid in 1876 during Prince of Wales' visit.

pois.name: Galtaji Temple (Monkey Temple & Holy Kunds)
pois.type: Ancient Rock-Cleft Temple Complex & Natural Springs
pois.description: Prehistoric Hindu pilgrimage retreat built into a narrow mountain pass with seven holy natural spring water tanks (kunds) and rhesus macaques.
pois.history: Established by Saint Galav in the 15th century as a meditative retreat of the Ramanuja sect.

pois.name: Patrika Gate (Jawahar Circle)
pois.description: Dazzling 9-arch entrance gate inside Asia's largest circular park, with every corridor ceiling hand-painted with Rajasthani frescoes.
pois.history: Constructed by the Patrika Group as the ninth gate of Jaipur celebrating Rajasthan's artistic legacy.

pois.name: Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple)
pois.type: Pure White Makrana Marble Modern Temple
pois.description: Pure white Makrana marble temple sitting at the foot of Moti Dungri hill, adorned with intricate marble carvings of mythological scenes and philosophers.
pois.history: Built in 1988 by the B.M. Birla Foundation on land allocated by the Maharaja of Jaipur for a token one rupee.

pois.name: Rambagh Palace Jaipur
pois.type: Former Royal Residence & World's Top Luxury Palace Hotel
pois.description: Palatial residence of the Maharaja of Jaipur set in 47 acres of tranquil gardens with peacocks, marble corridors, and Suvarna Mahal dining.
pois.history: Built in 1835, transformed into the residence of Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II and Maharani Gayatri Devi.

pois.name: The Oberoi Rajvilas Jaipur
pois.description: Sprawling 32-acre fort-style resort with sunken marble baths, luxury air-conditioned royal tents, and a 280-year-old Shiva temple.
pois.history: Masterpiece of luxury Rajasthani craftsmanship designed to recreate the opulence of Rajput princely encampments.

pois.name: Jai Mahal Palace (Taj)
pois.type: 1745 Indo-Saracenic Royal Palace in Mughal Gardens
pois.description: Stunning 1745 palace set in 18 acres of landscaped Mughal gardens with life-size outdoor chess, peacocks, and Cinnamon royal dining.
pois.history: Former residence of the Prime Minister of the princely state of Jaipur, exquisitely restored by Taj Hotels.

safetyZones.name: Chandani Chowk Highway Convergence
safetyZones.reason: Multi-tier flyover merger with rapid heavy vehicle transit towards Hinjawadi and Bengaluru bypass.
safetyZones.recommendedPrecaution: Maintain speed under 40 km/h; use dedicated service lanes for Kothrud turnoffs.

safetyZones.name: Alka Talkies Chowk & Riverside Road
safetyZones.reason: Mutha riverbed road prone to sudden water accumulation during Khadakwasla dam discharge.
safetyZones.recommendedPrecaution: Prefer Shivaji Road or Kelkar Road bypass during heavy monsoon discharge alerts.

safetyZones.name: Khadki Old Industrial Underpass
safetyZones.reason: Narrow underbridge with intermittent sodium lighting; isolated pedestrian pathway after 11 PM.
safetyZones.recommendedPrecaution: Prefer Pune-Mumbai Old Highway main arterial with 24/7 streetlights and cab movement.

safetyZones.name: University Circle (Ganeshkhind Road)
safetyZones.reason: Ongoing integrated Metro flyover construction causing slow peak-hour transit towards Aundh.
safetyZones.recommendedPrecaution: Use Senapati Bapat Road or Pashan link road to reach Baner during rush hours.

Deccan & FC Road.name: Deccan & FC Road
Deccan & FC Road.tagline: Academic Heritage, Student Culture & Street Food Heaven
Deccan & FC Road.summary: Vibrant pedestrian hub with 24/7 security, budget-friendly authentic food, and historic colleges.
topPros: High police patrolling & safe night walks
Deccan & FC Road.transitScore: Grade A+ (Metro Line 1 & 2, PMPML bus interchange)

Koregaon Park.name: Koregaon Park
Koregaon Park.tagline: Lush Green Canopies, Zen Sanctuaries & Global Cafes
Koregaon Park.summary: Tree-lined lanes, artisanal bakeries, upscale boutiques, and exceptional private community security.
Koregaon Park.transitScore: Grade A- (Airport road proximity, cabs, auto-rickshaws)

Shivajinagar & JM Road.name: Shivajinagar & JM Road
Shivajinagar & JM Road.tagline: Transit Epicenter, Pav Bhaji Strip & Civic Heart
Shivajinagar & JM Road.summary: Superb connectivity with multi-modal train, metro, and bus hubs; bustling dining stretch.

Baner & Balewadi.name: Baner & Balewadi
Baner & Balewadi.tagline: Modern IT Corridor, High Street & Rooftop Microbreweries
Baner & Balewadi.summary: Cosmopolitan IT lifestyle destination with modern infrastructure and buzzing weekend nightlife.
topCons: Highway merger delays at Chandani Chowk
Baner & Balewadi.transitScore: Grade B+ (Mumbai-Pune Expressway access, Metro Line 3 route)

Swargate & Camp.name: Swargate & Camp
Swargate & Camp.tagline: Colonial Bakeries, Sarasbaug Bhel & Wholesale Markets
Swargate & Camp.summary: Rich Parsi/colonial bakeries and unbeatable wholesale shopping with central bus connectivity.
Swargate & Camp.transitScore: Grade A (Swargate Bus Terminal, Underground Metro)

citizenReports.title: Fresh Shrewsbury Biscuits Batch & Acoustic Music
citizenReports.description: Lively evening crowd outside Camp bakeries. Safe walking environment, well-lit, open till 10:30 PM.
citizenReports.author: Citizen Rohan P.

citizenReports.title: Metro Barricade & Diversion on Ganeshkhind Rd
citizenReports.description: Single lane open towards University circle due to crane movement. 20-minute slow transit.
citizenReports.author: Priya D. (Commuter)

citizenReports.title: Pavement Tree Pruning & Dim Light on Lane 3
citizenReports.description: Municipal pruning branches on sidewalk. Use phone flashlights or walk on opposite cafe side.
citizenReports.author: Tanmay S.

trafficIndex.transitTip: Pune Metro Aqua Line & Purple Line recommended for Deccan to Civil Court transit.
